question: Should OpenClaw adopt `local`, `container`, `reverse-proxy`, and `node-mode` as the initial supported hosting-profile catalog once the readiness foundation is accepted?
rationale: The PR introduces new operator-facing configuration and support guarantees; source review cannot determine whether these four postures and their compatibility commitments match the intended product boundary.

options.title: Adopt the four-profile catalog
options.body: Accept the opt-in catalog after confirming RFC 0018 and require implementation work to preserve unprofiled upgrades and provide package-level conformance coverage.

options.title: Keep readiness profile-free
options.body: Accept or continue the underlying readiness work without committing to named deployment postures until support ownership and release guarantees are defined.

options.title: Narrow the catalog first
options.body: Request a revised RFC that limits v1 to the postures maintainers are willing to test and support as stable contracts.

recommendation.title: Adopt the four-profile catalog
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in catalog after confirming RFC 0018 and require implementation work to preserve unprofiled upgrades and provide package-level conformance coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The author owns the linked design rationale and can clarify boundaries, while the final decision remains with repository product leadership.
